title: A Closer Look at Q3 2026 Results
summary: Explore Target’s third quarter 2026 financial results with an infographic featuring highlights from the company’s earnings release.
body_markdown:
This morning, Target announced our third quarter 2026 earnings. Check out the[full results](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/11/target-corporation-reports-third-quarter-earnings) and read on for a snapshot.


## Our strategy continues to drive growth


+7.1%


**Net Sales Growth**


+5.6%


**Comparable Sales**


+5.0%


Traffic


$2.65


**GAAP & Adjusted1 EPS**


Which included the impact of tariff refunds. Excluding this impact, adjusted EPS increased 21% year-over-year.²


### Guests are choosing Target more often


-


We saw broad-based strength across the business, spanning income demographics, geographies, channels and categories.


-


Store comp sales grew 4.6% and digital comp sales were up 9.8%.


-


Sales grew across a majority of our core merchandising categories.


-


Non-merchandise sales grew nearly 20%, reflecting strong growth in Roundel, Target Circle Card, Target Circle 360 and Target Plus.


## The changes we’ve made are compounding to make Target a destination for discovery


Food & Beverage sales grew nearly 7%, driven by a differentiated assortment and the introduction of thousands of new items. Since the Q2 assortment reset, snacks, candy and beverages have collectively delivered nearly 10% net sales growth.


Beauty grew more than 9%, fueled by core beauty newness and exclusives in skincare, fragrance and haircare. Target Beauty Studio launched in 600+ stores, bringing together emerging and prestige brands in an elevated shopping and discovery experience.


Fun101 grew nearly 27%, with broad-based strength and share gains across the assortment driven by newness in our electronics owned brand, Heyday and record Pokémon sales. We also reinvented Fan Shops in more than 1,600 stores, nearly doubling space and assortment.


Our only-at-Target mix of style, newness and value resonated with busy families during the back-to-school and back-to-college seasons, resulting in mid-single-digit sales growth and market share gains.


### We’re making shopping at Target even easier and more affordable


- We lowered prices on nearly 2,000 home, apparel and accessories items in Q3, building on thousands of price reductions over the past year.
- Our investments in store payroll and training are driving further improvements in guest satisfaction, and on-shelf availability improved by a full percentage point year-over-year, including gains on our most frequently purchased items.
- Two-thirds of our digital business is driven by same-day services, with Same-Day Delivery growing at twice the rate of Order Pickup and Drive Up and reaching 80% of the U.S. population.
- We’re getting even faster across all types of fulfillment, with next-day shipping appearing twice as often at checkout compared to last year.


### We’re bringing the best of Target to even more communities


-


In 2026, we've opened[32 new stores](https://corporate.target.com/press/fact-sheet/2024/04/store-openings) and remodeled more than 130 stores.


-


With our new stores, we've entered 11 new markets and are reaching nearly 2 million additional guests while creating more than 5,000 new jobs.


## We’re bringing style, design and value to busy families this holiday season


#### More affordable gifts


We’ve introduced more than 8,000 new gifts, over half exclusive to Target. Most new holiday items are $20 or less, including thousands of gifts at $5 and under.


#### Making holiday shopping easier with technology


Ask Target helps guests discover products and shop with confidence, while AI-powered tools help teams improve availability and keep shelves stocked.


#### Bringing joy to our communities


Through Great Giftogether, our teams will help fulfill holiday wish lists for more than 4,500 families. Plus, for a limited time, $3 from every special-edition[Gigglescape St. Jude bear](https://www.target.com/p/holiday-2026-st-jude-bear-12-5-34-ivory-gigglescape-8482/-/A-1010032326) purchase supports St. Jude Children's Research Hospital.


## Finishing 2026 strong and continuing our investments in 2027


**With continued strong performance through Q3, Target has revised its full-year expectations**


**We are now planning for net sales growth in a range around 6%. We expect full-year EPS in a range of $10.65 to $11.40, which includes approximately $2.14 in tariff refund benefits recognized to date.3**


$5-6 billion


Expected in capital expenditures in 2027, compared with our expectation of ~$5 billion in 2026, as we continue investing for sustained, profitable growth.


1 Adjusted EPS is a non-GAAP financial measure most directly comparable to GAAP EPS. Adjusted EPS is reconciled to GAAP EPS in our Q3 2026 earnings release posted on our investor relations website. GAAP EPS increased 75 percent and Adjusted EPS increased 49 percent year-over-year, including tariff refund impacts.


2 Third quarter 2026 results include $301 million of pretax tariff refund benefits within gross margin and operating income, an after-tax contribution of $228 million to net earnings and $0.50 to both GAAP and Adjusted EPS. Excluding this impact, GAAP EPS increased 49% year-over-year.


3 The Company's guidance excludes any potential future tariff refunds.

Please see our Q3 earnings release and our SEC filings for risks and uncertainties that could cause Target’s results to differ materially from what was expected as of the date of this document, November 18, 2026.
